## Goal

Document the herdr worklist hydrator in packages/herdr/README.md so operators understand its cadence, semantics, safety, and why pane-title IDs must survive truncation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README documents: 30s cadence, immediate run on focus-resume, visibility gating (zero wl while hidden).
2. README documents demotion rules (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open) with the status/stage compatibility note.
3. README documents fail-open semantics (missing/unparseable CLI output → no demotions, never a crash).
4. README documents the pane-title ID-survival rationale (matching relies on ' - WL-<id>' in titles; pane-title amendment F0).
5. Docs match the shipped implementation (reviewed at close).

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/README.md

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a 'Hydrator' subsection under the worklist/downtime worker docs area with the bullets above.

## Dependencies

- Requires F2 (implementation facts) and F0 (format rationale)

## Summary

Add the drag-detection state, the pure drag mapper and a selection-preserving list scroll method — the core logic slice for WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK, covered by the test-first suite (C1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `MouseDragState` (press origin, fractional accumulator, active flag, pre-press `selectedIndex`/`scrollOffset`) and `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS = 1` are exported alongside `MouseClickState` (parent AC5)
- Pure `mapMouseDrag(state, ev, dragState, termSize)` returns `drag-start` on left-press, `drag-list` (whole rows) in list mode, `drag-detail` (lines) in detail mode, and null for sub-threshold, release and filter-mode input (parent AC1, AC2, AC5)
- `WorkItemListState.scrollBy(rows)` scrolls `scrollOffset` clamped to `[0, maxOffset]` using the same `_listHeight()`/`flatCount` maths as `_adjustScroll`, and never mutates `selectedIndex` (parent AC1, AC5)
- `mapMouseDrag` reports detail movement as whole-line deltas (1 terminal row ≈ 1 line) in `drag-detail`, leaving the existing detail clamp to the dispatcher (parent AC2)
- A fractional accumulator converts continuous movement into discrete row/line steps so content tracks the pointer with no sub-row artefacts (Desired change 3)
- All C1 tests covering the pure mapper, list drag and detail drag pass; no existing keyboard/state tests regress (parent AC6)

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `MouseDragState`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS` and the pure `mapMouseDrag` to `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` near `MouseClickState` / `mapMouseToAction`
- Add `WorkItemListState.scrollBy(rows)` reusing the `maxOffset` clamp from `_adjustScroll` / `_listHeight`, documented as selection-preserving
- Keep the mapper pure and unit-testable; use `state.getDisplayRows()` only for row bounds, not for side effects

## Dependencies

- C1 — Test: drag-to-scroll unit tests (WL test item defines expected behaviour)

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` changes (`MouseDragState`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS`, `mapMouseDrag`, `WorkItemListState.scrollBy`)
- Green tests for the pure mapper, list drag and detail drag

### Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts`

## Summary

Thread the drag tracker through `handleMouseInput`, dispatch drag actions (restoring the pre-press selection on activation), and split the motion branch of `mapMouseToAction` into hover (button-less) vs drag (left-held). Integration slice for WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `handleMouseInput` threads a `MouseDragState` (alongside `MouseClickState`), updating it on press/motion/release and dispatching `drag-start` / `drag-list` / `drag-detail` (parent AC1, AC2)
- On drag activation past the threshold the dispatcher restores the pre-press `selectedIndex` and `scrollOffset`, so a drag never leaves the selection moved by the initial press (parent AC3)
- The drag consumer never emits `select-row` / `open-detail`; drag releases are inert, so a drag-release can never click (parent AC3)
- Motion is split by the SGR button field: button-less motion (`(button & 3) === 3`) keeps the existing `hover-row` / `hover-none` mapping; left-button-held motion (`(button & 32) !== 0` and `(button & 3) === 0`) goes to the drag mapper; other buttons stay inert (parent AC4)
- `drag-list` calls `WorkItemListState.scrollBy(rows)`; `drag-detail` calls the existing `detailScrollUp` / `detailScrollDown` clamp; drag is inert in filter mode and in the metadata panel (parent AC2, constraints)
- Existing click, double-click, wheel, filter-tap, hover-tooltip, Alt+m and keyboard behaviours are unchanged and their tests pass (parent AC6)

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a `dragState` alongside `clickState` at the `runWorklistTui` call site and pass it into `handleMouseInput`
- Extend the `MouseAction` union and the `handleMouseInput` dispatch switch with `drag-list` / `drag-detail` (and the internal `drag-start` bookkeeping)
- Replace the `button & 32` branch in `mapMouseToAction` with hover (button-less) vs drag (left-held) routing, delegating to `mapMouseDrag`
- Record the pre-press selection/scroll on left-press and restore it on the first threshold crossing

## Dependencies

- C2 — Implement: drag state, pure mapper and list scroll

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` changes (drag dispatch, motion-branch split, pre-press restore)
- Green integration tests for drag dispatch and hover/drag separation

### Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts`
data.title: Implement: drag dispatch and hover/drag split

# Cooldown behaviour documentation

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Update all affected documentation so the model-cooldown contract, the
cheap-switch gate and the bounded wake are discoverable and unambiguous, and so
the withdrawn client-drain constraint is recorded where a future change would
see it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC7 — Documentation: all related documentation is updated to reflect the cooldown changes, including code comments and the herdr README.
- [ ] The on-disk cooldown contract (file, schemaVersion, fields, tolerance) is documented in one place with cross-references from both consuming packages.
- [ ] The fail-closed direction (an unreadable signal means no cheap switch) and the bounded default are documented as explicit behaviour.
- [ ] The withdrawn client-drain constraint is recorded so a future change cannot silently regress it.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC7 (parent AC7 "Documentation"): covers code comments, the herdr README, the
  mode-switch design doc and the downtime-dispatcher dev doc — one section per
  surface, each pointing at the shared contract module rather than restating the
  field list.
- Single source of truth: the shared module header describes the fields and
  tolerance rules; the other documents link to it.
- Fail-closed and bounded default: state the direction explicitly (unreadable ⇒
  hold fast; absent ⇒ normal decision) and the clamp values.
- Regression guard: a short "must not regress" note citing the withdrawn
  predecessor records the constraint next to the behaviour it constrains.

## Deliverables

- Updated code comments in both packages.
- Updated `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md` and
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- Updated `packages/herdr/README.md`.
- Cross-references from every surface to the single contract of record.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/README.md`
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`

## Dependencies

Depends on `Recovery loop records durable cooldown`, `Cheap-switch gate honours
model cooldowns`, `Bounded wake of one cooled-down job` and `Bounded default
cooldown and fail-closed hardening`.

# Cooldown regression guard and full-suite verification

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Prove the withdrawn client-side drain has not been reintroduced and that the
whole project suite passes with the cooldown changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC6 — Tests: unit + integration tests cover detection, gating, wake, cross-root and failure paths.
- [ ] AC8 — Full-suite: the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] Regression guard: a regression test proves the withdrawn client drain is not reintroduced.
- [ ] Baseline: the suite test count and runtime before and after are recorded in a work-item comment.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC6 (parent AC6 "Tests"): the covered paths are detection (exhaustion
  classification), gating (cheap-switch hold), wake (bounded resume),
  cross-root (two-root integration) and the failure paths (unreadable signal,
  unwritable marker, absent Retry-After).
- AC8 (parent AC8 "Full-suite"): run the project suite command from the
  repository root and require a clean pass.
- Regression guard specifics: assert there is no client-side slot-count
  completion gate, no dispatch pause and no unbounded latch in the new paths —
  the three things the withdrawn predecessor
  (`WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR`) removed.
- Baseline: record the pre-change and post-change totals so suite drift is
  visible.

## Deliverables

- The regression test proving the withdrawn drain is not reintroduced.
- A recorded full-suite run (count and runtime before/after).
- The baseline comment on the parent work item.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-loop.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`

## Dependencies

Depends on `Recovery loop records durable cooldown`, `Cheap-switch gate honours
model cooldowns`, `Bounded wake of one cooled-down job` and `Bounded default
cooldown and fail-closed hardening`.
